---
title: "What is associated with the gap?"
---

The latest-period driver analysis includes 3,023 hospitals with reportable OP-18b and OP-18c scores and at least 11 sampled patients in each. The baseline model adjusts for hospital type, ownership, emergency-service status, metro status, and state fixed effects. Critical Access Hospitals have an estimated gap 17.3 minutes smaller than acute care hospitals (95% CI 7.3–27.2 minutes smaller) in this specification.

An expanded model adds certified beds, psychiatric-unit beds, and county mental-health HPSA designation. The CAH estimate attenuates to 12.3 minutes lower, with an interval from 27.9 minutes lower to 3.3 minutes higher. The expanded model explains 5.8% of observed variation, compared with 5.7% in the baseline. The added variables do not make this a causal model.

CMS bed counts come from the 2026 Q2 Provider of Services file. HRSA HPSA designations are current at retrieval and were joined by county FIPS; all 3,023 hospitals have a valid county FIPS. A county with no currently designated geographic record is coded No. This is not hospital-specific workforce availability. These sources postdate the September 2025 outcome. Psychiatric-unit beds do not measure the full supply of nearby beds. Ownership uses Voluntary non-profit - Private as its reference; federal, physician, and tribal ownership are grouped as Other.

Peer groups are set by CMS hospital type and USDA 2023 metro status, not by outcomes. See the [full driver report](../results/hospital_driver_analysis.md), [expanded coefficients](../results/hospital_driver_model_coefficients.csv), [baseline coefficients](../results/hospital_driver_model_base_coefficients.csv), and [hospital-to-peer file](../results/hospital_peer_comparison.csv). These results are not hospital quality rankings.
